reason: The text demonstrates the opposite of the statement. While Yahweh does address Moses and Aaron as leaders, the narrative consistently shows Yahweh's empathy and care directed toward the entire people of Israel. Key evidence includes: (1) Yahweh giving 'the people' favor in the eyes of the Egyptians (וַֽיהוָ֞ה נָתַ֨ן אֶת־ חֵ֥ן הָעָ֛ם); (2) the detailed Passover ordinances established 'for all the congregation of Israel' (כָּל־ עֲדַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יַעֲשׂ֥וּ אֹתֽוֹ); (3) Yahweh's direct action bringing out 'all the children of Israel' from Egypt (הוֹצִ֨יא יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל); and (4) protective laws even for sojourners and purchased servants. The leaders serve as intermediaries through whom Yahweh expresses care for the entire nation, not recipients of exclusive divine concern.
